# codespec CLI

Generated by `codespec-docs` from the clap definition in [`crates/cli/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/main/crates/cli/src/lib.rs). It lists only commands that exist. `codespec --version` prints the version, and `--help` after any command prints the same text.

> Read code into cir/1, check it, write code from it

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`codespec validate`](#codespec-validate) | Validate a cir/1 document; with --canonical, also require its canonical encoding |
| [`codespec schema`](#codespec-schema) | Print the JSON Schema of cir/1 |
| [`codespec features`](#codespec-features) | Print the cir/1 feature vocabulary (codespec-features/1): every feature id an adapter can support, sorted by id |
| [`codespec read`](#codespec-read) | Run the reader adapter for LANG over SOURCE and write the validated cir/1 module to OUT |
| [`codespec pass`](#codespec-pass) | Apply every pass (lookup-guard, then the facts) to a cir/1 module and write the result to OUT |
| [`codespec write`](#codespec-write) | Validate a cir/1 module and run the writer adapter for LANG, writing into OUT |
| [`codespec conform`](#codespec-conform) | Run the conformance kit against the adapter codespec-ROLE-LANG, by the claim its --describe manifest prints, and write a codespec-conformance-report/1 to OUT; exit 1 when it does not conform. With --check REPORT, run again for the report's adapter and exit 1 naming every feature whose entry differs |
| [`codespec measure`](#codespec-measure) | Measure a reader's output: counts read and refused functions per artefact by refusal category, then the totals and the share read |
| [`codespec effects`](#codespec-effects) | Report what each function of one module, or of several read as one program, may do outside its own memory: per function, its effects (db, env, fs.read, fs.write, io, net, proc, rand, stdin, stdout, time), with a barrier the syscalls it reaches, where each comes from, and every reason that set may be incomplete, as codespec-effects-report/1 |
| [`codespec reach`](#codespec-reach) | List, per module, the functions the entry functions reach and those they do not, as codespec-reach-report/1: the tree-shaking result and the dead-code report |
| [`codespec trace`](#codespec-trace) | Print the call tree from one function as codespec-trace/1: its statements, each if, switch and loop a branch node with its condition, each call expanded into the callee's tree, a call through an interface or a function value a dispatch node listing every candidate, syscalls and summarised externs at the leaves |
| [`codespec check`](#codespec-check) | Run one built-in defect check over modules read as one program and print one finding per line: position, function, check and the evidence it matched (the calls and their positions). Exit 0 with no finding, 1 with findings, 2 on an input error |
| [`codespec harness`](#codespec-harness) | Build every implementation EXAMPLE/harness.toml lists, run each on one generated trace per seed and require byte-equal output; exit 1 naming the seed, implementation and first differing line otherwise |

## `codespec validate`

Validate a cir/1 document; with --canonical, also require its canonical encoding

```text
Usage: codespec validate [OPTIONS] <FILE>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<FILE>` | yes | none | none | The cir/1 document to read. |
| `--canonical` | no | none | none | Also require the file's bytes to be the document's canonical encoding. |

## `codespec schema`

Print the JSON Schema of cir/1

```text
Usage: codespec schema
```

## `codespec features`

Print the cir/1 feature vocabulary (codespec-features/1): every feature id an adapter can support, sorted by id

```text
Usage: codespec features
```

## `codespec read`

Run the reader adapter for LANG over SOURCE and write the validated cir/1 module to OUT

```text
Usage: codespec read --lang <LANG> --out <OUT> --adapters <ADAPTERS> <SOURCE>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--lang <LANG>` | yes | none | none | The source language; selects the adapter `codespec-read-<lang>`. |
| `<SOURCE>` | yes | none | none | The source the adapter reads: for Go, one package directory. |
| `--out <OUT>` | yes | none | none | Where the validated cir/1 module is written, in canonical encoding. |
| `--adapters <ADAPTERS>` | yes | none | `CODESPEC_ADAPTERS` | Directory holding the adapter programs `codespec-read-<lang>` and `codespec-write-<lang>`. |

## `codespec pass`

Apply every pass (lookup-guard, then the facts) to a cir/1 module and write the result to OUT

```text
Usage: codespec pass --out <OUT> <FILE>
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<FILE>` | yes | none | none | The cir/1 module to rewrite. |
| `--out <OUT>` | yes | none | none | Where the rewritten module is written, in canonical encoding. |

## `codespec write`

Validate a cir/1 module and run the writer adapter for LANG, writing into OUT

```text
Usage: codespec write --lang <LANG> --out <OUT> --adapters <ADAPTERS> <FILE>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--lang <LANG>` | yes | none | none | The target language; selects the adapter `codespec-write-<lang>`. |
| `<FILE>` | yes | none | none | The cir/1 module to write. |
| `--out <OUT>` | yes | none | none | The directory the adapter writes into. |
| `--adapters <ADAPTERS>` | yes | none | `CODESPEC_ADAPTERS` | Directory holding the adapter programs `codespec-read-<lang>` and `codespec-write-<lang>`. |

## `codespec conform`

Run the conformance kit against the adapter codespec-ROLE-LANG, by the claim its --describe manifest prints, and write a codespec-conformance-report/1 to OUT; exit 1 when it does not conform. With --check REPORT, run again for the report's adapter and exit 1 naming every feature whose entry differs

```text
Usage: codespec conform [OPTIONS] --adapters <ADAPTERS>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--lang <LANG>` | no | none | none | The adapter's language; selects codespec-ROLE-LANG and the runner codespec-run-LANG. |
| `--role <ROLE>` | no | none | none | reader or writer. |
| `--out <OUT>` | no | none | none | Where the report is written; a missing directory is created. |
| `--check <CHECK>` | no | none | none | A report to check: run again and compare. |
| `--kit <KIT>` | no | `conformance` | none | The kit directory: kit.json and cases/. |
| `--corpus <CORPUS>` | no | none | none | A reader's corpus: one directory per kit case, its source and calls.json. Defaults to KIT/reader/LANG. |
| `--adapters <ADAPTERS>` | yes | none | `CODESPEC_ADAPTERS` | Directory holding the adapter, its runner and, for a reader, codespec-write-go and codespec-run-go. |
| `--work <WORK>` | no | none | none | Where each case is written, read and built; emptied first. Defaults to target/conform/ROLE-LANG. |
| `--timeout <TIMEOUT>` | no | `300` | none | Seconds one program (adapter, runner) may run before it is killed and the case recorded as `timeout`. |

## `codespec measure`

Measure a reader's output: counts read and refused functions per artefact by refusal category, then the totals and the share read. An artefact is a source file, the part of a position before its last `:`. A function is read when its body holds no `foreign` statement and refused when it holds one; a refusal outside every function counts under its file and category, and is a refused function too when it refuses a method's declaration (a call shape `T(…)` or `T.m(…)`, such as a Groovy hook `T.methodMissing(…)`). A constructor `New<T>` a JVM reader made at its class's position is not counted. The category is the text of the refusal's reason before the first `: ` when it is one of the Groovy reader's eight (dynamic, closure, groovy-semantics, type, unresolved, gorm, spring, unsupported), and uncategorised otherwise. Files and categories are in byte order; the same document gives the same bytes.

```text
Usage: codespec measure [OPTIONS] <MODULE>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<MODULE>` | yes | none | none | The module to measure: a cir/1 document. |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | no | `text` | none | text, a table with one row per artefact; or json, codespec-measure/1 in canonical encoding. |

## `codespec effects`

Report what each function of one module, or of several read as one program, may do outside its own memory: per function, its effects (db, env, fs.read, fs.write, io, net, proc, rand, stdin, stdout, time), with a barrier the syscalls it reaches, where each comes from, and every reason that set may be incomplete, as codespec-effects-report/1. A function's effects are those of every extern it calls, as the summaries state them, of println (stdout), of every syscall it reaches, and of every function or method it calls, to a fixed point over all modules given. An extern naming the import path of a module given is a call of that module's function; a call through an interface or a function value reaches every function of the set that could stand there. An extern no summary names, a foreign statement whose calls are not listed, a method on a type no module declares, a function without a body the barrier does not resolve, and a call of a function that has one of these, are each listed as unknown with a position, never taken as pure. The same modules, summaries and barrier give the same bytes.

```text
Usage: codespec effects [OPTIONS] <MODULES>...
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<MODULES>` | yes | none | none | The modules to analyse, cir/1 documents, read as one program. |
| `--summaries <FILE>` | no | none | none | A codespec-effects/1 summary of functions outside the modules; repeat for several. Where two name one function, the first counts. |
| `--barrier <FILE>` | no | none | none | A codespec-barrier/1 document: the functions that enter the operating system and what each syscall does. |
| `--report <MODULE>` | no | none | none | Report only the module with this import path or name; repeat for several. All when absent. |
| `--roots` | no | none | none | Also count, per reported function, the unknown reasons of every function it reaches. |
| `--entry <FUNC>` | no | none | none | An entry function, `<path>.<name>` or `<path>.<type>.<method>`; repeat for several. With an entry, dispatch defaults to rta. |
| `--exported <MODULE>` | no | none | none | A module, by import path or name, whose every exported function is an entry; repeat for several. |
| `--dispatch <DISPATCH>` | no | none | none | How a call through an interface or a function value is resolved: cha, every candidate of the set (the default without entries); rta, only the types the code reached from the entries makes and the function values it uses (the default with entries). |

## `codespec reach`

List, per module, the functions the entry functions reach and those they do not, as codespec-reach-report/1: the tree-shaking result and the dead-code report. A function is reached by a call, by being used as a value, or as a candidate of a call through an interface or a function value. The entries are every --entry, every exported function of each --exported module, or when neither is given `main.main`; every Go init function and every module's variable initializers are entries too. An entry naming no function of the set is refused. The same modules give the same bytes.

```text
Usage: codespec reach [OPTIONS] <MODULES>...
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<MODULES>` | yes | none | none | The modules to analyse, cir/1 documents, read as one program. |
| `--entry <FUNC>` | no | none | none | An entry function, `<path>.<name>` or `<path>.<type>.<method>`; repeat for several. |
| `--exported <MODULE>` | no | none | none | A module, by import path or name, whose every exported function is an entry. |
| `--dispatch <DISPATCH>` | no | `rta` | none | cha: every candidate of the set; rta (default): only types made and function values used by reached code. |
| `--report <MODULE>` | no | none | none | List only the module with this import path or name; repeat for several. |

## `codespec trace`

Print the call tree from one function as codespec-trace/1: its statements, each if, switch and loop a branch node with its condition, each call expanded into the callee's tree, a call through an interface or a function value a dispatch node listing every candidate, syscalls and summarised externs at the leaves. Calls are resolved as `codespec effects` resolves them, over all modules given, with --from the only entry for rta. Each function is expanded once, where it is called fewest calls from --from; every other call of it is a ref node. A function more than --depth calls from --from is a cut node. Whatever `codespec effects` lists as unknown is an unknown node where it occurs. --from naming no function of the set is refused. The same modules, summaries and barrier give the same bytes.

```text
Usage: codespec trace [OPTIONS] --from <FUNC> <MODULES>...
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<MODULES>` | yes | none | none | The modules to analyse, cir/1 documents, read as one program. |
| `--from <FUNC>` | yes | none | none | The function the tree starts from, `<path>.<name>` or `<path>.<type>.<method>`. |
| `--depth <DEPTH>` | no | `8` | none | How many calls deep functions are expanded. |
| `--summaries <FILE>` | no | none | none | A codespec-effects/1 summary of functions outside the modules; repeat for several. |
| `--barrier <FILE>` | no | none | none | A codespec-barrier/1 document: the functions that enter the operating system and what each syscall does. |
| `--dispatch <DISPATCH>` | no | `rta` | none | cha: every candidate of the set; rta (default): only types made and function values used by code reached from --from. |

## `codespec check`

Run one built-in defect check over modules read as one program and print one finding per line: position, function, check and the evidence it matched (the calls and their positions). Exit 0 with no finding, 1 with findings, 2 on an input error. A check reads only cir/1: read bodies, the call lists of foreign statements and opaque functions, method sets and types. --list prints every check, one line on what it finds, and the name lists it matches calls against; --names replaces lists. What each check matches exactly is the crate doc of b10x-codespec-check.

```text
Usage: codespec check [OPTIONS] [CHECK] [MODULES]...
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<CHECK>` | no | none | none | The check to run; --list names them. |
| `<MODULES>` | no | none | none | The modules to check, cir/1 documents, read as one program. |
| `--list` | no | none | none | Print every check, what it finds and its name lists, and exit. |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | no | `text` | none | text, one line per finding; or json, codespec-check-report/1. |
| `--strict` | no | none | none | insecure-random: report every call into a random package. |
| `--names <FILE>` | no | none | none | A JSON object of list name to an array of entries, each replacing that list. |
| `--report <MODULE>` | no | none | none | Report only findings in the module with this import path or name, or under it; repeat for several. All when absent. |
| `--entry <FUNC>` | no | none | none | unreached: an entry function, `<path>.<name>` or `<path>.<type>.<method>`; repeat for several. |
| `--exported <MODULE>` | no | none | none | unreached: a module, by import path or name, whose every exported function is an entry; repeat for several. |

## `codespec harness`

Build every implementation EXAMPLE/harness.toml lists, run each on one generated trace per seed and require byte-equal output; exit 1 naming the seed, implementation and first differing line otherwise

```text
Usage: codespec harness [OPTIONS] <EXAMPLE>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Environment | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<EXAMPLE>` | yes | none | none | The example directory holding harness.toml. |
| `--seeds <SEEDS>` | no | `200` | none | How many seeds, 0 to SEEDS-1, each giving one trace. |
| `--commands <COMMANDS>` | no | `300` | none | Commands per trace. |
| `--build-dir <BUILD_DIR>` | no | `target/harness` | none | Directory the implementations are built into; `{build}` in harness.toml. |

## Exit status

0 on success. 1 when a document is refused (unknown field, unknown kind, an untyped expression, another format, not canonical under `--canonical`), when an adapter is missing, exits non-zero or prints a document the model refuses, and when the harness finds a difference; the reason is printed on stderr as `codespec: <reason>`. Clap's own usage errors exit 2.
